methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); net revenue, credit cost, expense, nonperforming-asset and pre-tax margin signals with JPMorgan Chase's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'JPMorgan Chase & Co. ... is a leading financial services firm based in the United States' 'Unfavorable market and economic conditions could adversely affect JPMorganChase’s wholesale businesses.' 'JPMorganChase operates in a highly competitive environment in which it must constantly adapt to changes in financial regulation, technological advances and economic conditions.' (FY2025 10-K); DURABLE, risk 2: the 10-K ties results to markets and the economy, a cycle and a competitive field, and does not call its own business cyclical (the word appears only in 'countercyclical capital buffer', a regulatory term: the LOW and SHW reading); among its competitors it lists 'e-commerce and other internet-based companies, digital asset and other financial technology companies', and among the products non-depository institutions offer 'cryptocurrency, including stablecoins'; a new risk factor says 'JPMorganChase’s operations, results, and competitive standing could be adversely affected by the development of advanced technologies such as AI.', among its risks 'replacement or disintermediation of direct customer relationships if AI agents autonomously manage or intermediate financial decisions and product selection or other services for customers' (GENAI is live, but its registered scope is software seats, IT services and BPO hours, professional information, search, education content and mobility, which names no bank, so these words stay here: the PEP obesity rule; widening the scope is the owner's call); it says 'both financial institutions and their non-banking competitors face the risk of disruption to payments processing and other products and services from the use of new technologies that may not require intermediation, such as tokenized securities or other products that leverage distributed ledger technology'; CRYPTO is live (from 2020-10-21) and scoped to banks and payments: these words put it on the watch list, company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for JPMorgan Chase

theme_watch.reason: Live: JPMorgan Chase's own FY2025 10-K says 'both financial institutions and their non-banking competitors face the risk of disruption to payments processing and other products and services from the use of new technologies that may not require intermediation, such as tokenized securities or other products that leverage distributed ledger technology'. The stock trades at 15.5x FY26E — a premium. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (CRYPTO) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing crypto disintermediation of JPMorgan Chase's payments and banking specifically.

BEAR.desc: EPS -21.3%/yr (worst year FY16-FY25, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +10.3%/yr (Q4 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +13.9%/yr (FY16-FY25 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +24.9%/yr (best 2-yr run FY16-FY25, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: JPM (retrospective, 2026-04-10) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 8.53x (62.8% downside to Bear $115.32 / +7.4% upside to Bull $332.67) | Adj composite 1.93 vs market 3.63: gap -1.70 [OVERVALUED] | +72% above the EPP floor $180.18 (9x FY26E $20.02) | Conservative 2-yr case: -12.7% total (-6.3%/yr) | At 15.5x FY26E the 15% hurdle price $409.80 sits above the BULL case; revenue +7.1% YoY in Q4 2025, forward revenues +7.1% (Q4 2025 revenue growth (no Q1 2026 guide)); crypto is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
